records.text: Abraham Polak wrote a researched book arguing that Israelis descend from the Khazar tribe that converted to Judaism.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But if you read books that were printed in Israel by the Israelis, they themselves declared that they were Khazarian. You could look at a guy named Abraham Polak as an example, who wrote a book, did all the research, was awarded for his research, and said, hey, we're that tribe.

verification.notes: Poliak's book and contemporary discussion support his Khazar-origin hypothesis for much of Eastern European Jewry, but the statement overgeneralizes this into a claim about Israelis as a whole.

sources.title: You Don't Have to Be Khazarian? | The New York Review of Books
sources.relevance: Describes Poliak's argument that Khazars were ancestors of much of Eastern European Jewry.

sources.title: Khazaria: History of a Jewish Kingdom in Europe | National Library of Israel
sources.relevance: Authoritative catalog record for Abraham Poliak's book.

records.text: Owens said Abraham Polak won awards for tracing Ashkenazi Jews to the Khazars
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's about the origin of the Ashkenazi Jews, the Khazars. ... Look up Abraham Polak. He won awards for saying they were the Khazars and tracing them back.

verification.notes: Personal statements and private interactions cannot be publicly verified.
